title: Route map journey (Canvas)
description: A stylised journey map on real coastlines (Natural Earth 1:50m land, public domain, Web Mercator). Stops are placed from latitude/longitude; the camera eases to frame each leg while a dot or plane marker draws the route (arc or straight), a ripple and a stop card fire on each arrival, and distance and duration counters count up to their stated totals in proportion to great-circle leg length. The outro pulls back to the whole labelled route. Portrait stacks title, map and counters; landscape adds an itinerary panel. Land can be filled, a dot matrix, or omitted for an abstract map.

title.description: Title of the journey, shown above the map (portrait) or in the panel (landscape)

stops.description: Place names in travel order; empty strings are skipped (at least two must be non-empty)

notes.description: Optional one-line detail on each stop's card (same order as stops; empty for none)

lat.description: Latitude of each stop in decimal degrees (south negative), same order as stops. A named stop at exactly 0, 0 is treated as missing coordinates and fails the render

lon.description: Longitude of each stop in decimal degrees (west negative), same order as stops

distance.description: Total distance shown by the counter at the end (0 hides the distance counter). Shown exactly as given; legs share it in proportion to great-circle length

duration.description: Total duration shown by the second counter at the end (0 hides it)

labels.description: Small labels above the two counters

path.description: Leg shape: arc (flight-style curve) or straight (rhumb line). Neither follows real roads or rails

marker.description: Travelling marker: a pulsing dot or a plane silhouette that turns with the route

land.description: Land style: fill (solid coastlines), dots (dot-matrix land) or none (abstract map: graticule only, no geography)

borders.description: Draw international land boundaries (Natural Earth de facto lines; disputed lines are omitted) as faint dashes

palette.description: Sea (ground), land, ink, accent (route, marker, chips), muted (labels, dashed route ahead) and card colours

license: MIT (code); map data public domain (Natural Earth)
notes: Land outlines: Natural Earth 1:50m Land (ne_50m_land.geojson from github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector, VERSION 5.2.0-pre, downloaded 2026-10-18, sha256 0e874b27a51d146452be360cafb3cc50c86001074a67d534113e6534682f9826b). Natural Earth states: 'All versions of Natural Earth raster + vector map data found on this website are in the public domain' (naturalearthdata.com/about/terms-of-use). Made with Natural Earth.

Borders: Natural Earth 1:50m Admin 0 boundary lines (ne_50m_admin_0_boundary_lines_land.geojson, same source and version, sha256 2faac4f6b34386f3d21b6e018cf151f241f00e5c936d44dd17d7d9bfb147fa48), public domain. Only features classed 'International boundary (verify)' are kept; Natural Earth draws de facto boundaries, so a reviewer should confirm they suit the audience, or set borders to false.

land-50m.js and borders-50m.js were produced by build_map_data.py in this directory: Douglas-Peucker simplification at 0.015 degrees for land and 0.02 degrees for borders, land rings under 0.0005 square degrees (about 6 km²) dropped, coordinates quantised to 1/100 degree and delta encoded (land 60,669 -> 39,378 points; borders 18,955 -> 8,324).

Routes are stylised: arcs and rhumb lines between stops, not real roads, rails or flight paths. Distances and durations are shown exactly as given; the recipe never computes or claims them. Coastlines at this scale are coarse below about 2 degrees of span, so the camera never zooms in further.
land: none renders an abstract map with no geography; stop positions still follow the latitude/longitude params.

Beats: intro = min(1.4, 0.1 D); outro = min(2.8, 0.2 D); leg = (D - intro - outro) / (stops - 1); leg k starts at intro + k * leg, departs at +0.10 leg and arrives (ripple, card) at +0.60 leg (+0.78 leg when there are only two stops); the first stop's card appears at 0.55 * intro; the pull-back starts at D - outro.
Needs `pip install playwright` and `playwright install chromium-headless-shell`. Uses the system's Inter when installed.
